newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real rises 0.02 pct in seesaw trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real rises 0.02 pct in seesaw trade.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.02 percent to close at 1.0680 per dollar in seesaw trade on the commercial foreign exchange market with players concerned about dollar flows, dealers said.

After commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $142.7 million deficit Tuesday, the market had expected another day of dollar outflows, causing the local currency to drop to 1.0691 per dollar early Wednesday.

Dollar inflows, however, led the real to recover some ground later in the day, although expectations of a decline in the reais-dollar mini-band prevented the real from rising much further, dealers said.
The current mini-band was set by the Central Bank on Friday at between 1.0660 and 1.0710 reais per dollar. Market traders expect a new lowering of the mini-band any time soon.
At 1640 local/1940 GMT, preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $215 million surplus on Wednesday.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0711 per dollar, down 0.01 percent. In the parallel market, the real closed flat at 1.130 per dollar, traders said.
